_meta.description: Finding-category knowledge base. Identifiers only from MITRE ATT&CK v20 (Enterprise + ICS), MITRE D3FEND 1.6.0, OWASP WSTG v4.2 (versioned IDs), CWE. All prose is original wording of this project.

vulnerable-software.title: Outdated software with known vulnerabilities
fix: Confirm the exact installed version and the vendor advisory for every CVE listed.
Apply the vendor fixed release (or the supported LTS branch) through the normal change process; emergency change if the CVE is in CISA KEV.
If patching must wait, apply the vendor workaround or put the service behind an allowlist / WAF virtual patch and document the compensating control with an expiry date.
Add the component to the software inventory (SBOM / CMDB) so the next advisory is matched automatically.
verify: Re-run the version detection scan (nmap -sV --script vulners) and confirm the banner or package reports the fixed version.
Re-run the original exploit check (non-destructive) and confirm it fails.
vulnerable-software.detect: Alert on exploitation patterns for the listed CVEs at the edge (WAF/IDS) and on unexpected child processes of the service.

exposed-remote-access.title: Remote administration service reachable from untrusted networks
fix: Remove the direct exposure: close the port on the perimeter firewall / security group for any source outside the admin allowlist.
Publish remote administration only through the corporate VPN or a zero-trust access broker with MFA.
Enforce Network Level Authentication (RDP) or key-only authentication (SSH) and disable password logins for privileged accounts.
Record the rule change with ticket ID in the firewall change log.
verify: From an external vantage point, nmap -Pn -p <port> <public IP> must report filtered/closed.
Confirm the service is still reachable through the VPN / broker path for authorised admins.
exposed-remote-access.detect: SOC: alert on successful logons to this service from non-VPN source ranges and on password-spray patterns.

cleartext-protocol.title: Cleartext management or file-transfer protocol in use
fix: Replace Telnet with SSH and FTP with SFTP/FTPS; disable the cleartext daemon after migration.
Rotate every credential that was ever used over the cleartext protocol.
Block the cleartext port at the host firewall so it cannot be re-enabled silently.
verify: nmap -p 21,23 <host> must report closed/filtered.
Confirm that the replacement encrypted service accepts logins with rotated credentials.
cleartext-protocol.detect: SOC: network sensor rule for any new Telnet/FTP session on the segment.

legacy-smb.title: Legacy SMBv1 enabled / SMB exposed
fix: Disable SMBv1 on the server and clients (Windows feature removal or GPO) after checking that no legacy device still depends on it.
Install the cumulative security update that covers the listed CVEs.
Restrict TCP 445 to the subnets that need file services; never expose it to the internet or to the OT zone.
verify: nmap -p445 --script smb-protocols <host> must not list SMBv1 (NT LM 0.12).
nmap -p445 --script smb-vuln-ms17-010 <host> must report not vulnerable.
legacy-smb.detect: SOC: alert on SMBv1 negotiation and on lateral SMB connections between workstations.

exposed-database.title: Database or cache service reachable without network restriction
fix: Bind the service to the application subnet only and add a host firewall rule allowing just the app servers.
Require authentication and TLS for every client connection; remove anonymous or default accounts.
Move the database into a dedicated data tier segment if it currently shares the user VLAN.
verify: From a user-VLAN host, nmap -p <db port> <host> must report filtered.
Unauthenticated connection attempt must be refused.
exposed-database.detect: SOC: alert on database logins from hosts outside the application tier.

snmp-weak-community.title: SNMP v1/v2c with default or guessable community string
fix: Migrate the device to SNMPv3 with authPriv (SHA-2 + AES).
If v2c must stay temporarily, set a long random read-only community and an ACL that allows only the NMS address.
Disable SNMP write access entirely.
verify: nmap -sU -p161 --script snmp-info <host> with 'public' must fail.
NMS still polls the device over SNMPv3.
snmp-weak-community.detect: SOC: alert on SNMP requests from sources other than the NMS.

ot-protocol-exposed.title: Industrial control protocol reachable from outside the OT zone
fix: Do NOT scan aggressively or patch live controllers: open a Management of Change (MOC) with Process Safety before any intervention.

Contain first: add a deny rule at the IT/OT boundary (conduit) so the protocol is only reachable from the engineering workstations and historian in the OT DMZ (zones and conduits model, IEC 62443 style).
Enable the controller's write-protection / run-mode key or protocol allowlist where the vendor supports it.
Plan the permanent fix (firmware, segmentation redesign) for the next scheduled turnaround and record it in the plant maintenance system.
verify: Passive check: from the corporate IT VLAN, a single TCP connect test (nc -zv <ip> <port>) must fail; no active protocol scanning on production.
OT-ENG confirms with the asset owner that HMI/historian communication is unaffected (sign-off in MOC).
ot-protocol-exposed.detect: SOC + OT-ENG: passive OT network monitoring rule for any IT-sourced Modbus/S7/DNP3/EtherNet-IP session, and for write/program-download function codes.

weak-tls.title: Weak TLS configuration (old protocol versions or ciphers)
fix: Disable SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1; keep TLS 1.2 with AEAD ciphers and TLS 1.3.
Replace self-signed or expiring certificates with certificates from the corporate or public CA and automate renewal.
Apply the change through a shared hardening baseline (Ansible/GPO) so every web front end gets it.
verify: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p443 <host> must show no TLS 1.0/1.1 and grade A ciphers only.
testssl.sh <host> shows no high or critical items.
weak-tls.detect: Low detection value; track through configuration compliance scanning.

web-injection.title: Injection in web application (SQL / OS command)
fix: Replace string-built queries/commands with parameterised queries or safe APIs in the affected endpoint and in every endpoint that reuses the same data-access helper.
Add server-side input validation (allowlist of type, length, format).
Run the database account with least privilege (no DDL, no file or OS access).
Add a regression test reproducing the payload to the CI pipeline and a SAST rule for the pattern.
verify: Re-run the original proof of concept request; the response must not change behaviour or leak data.
DAST (ZAP active scan) on the endpoint reports no injection alert; CI regression test passes.
web-injection.detect: SOC: WAF/application log rule for SQL error strings and injection payload signatures on this endpoint.

web-xss.title: Cross-site scripting (reflected or stored)
fix: Apply context-aware output encoding in the template layer for the affected parameter (HTML, attribute, JS, URL contexts).
Enable the framework's auto-escaping and remove any raw/unsafe rendering helpers in the affected view.
Deploy a restrictive Content-Security-Policy (no unsafe-inline) as defence in depth.
Set HttpOnly on session cookies so injected script cannot read them.
verify: Replay the payload; it must render as inert text.
ZAP passive + active scan shows no XSS alert for the endpoint.
web-xss.detect: SOC: CSP violation reports forwarded to SIEM; alert on spikes.

broken-access-control.title: Broken access control (IDOR / BOLA)
fix: Enforce an object-level authorization check on the server for every request that takes an object identifier (owner or tenant match).
Centralise the check in a policy middleware instead of per-controller code.
Use non-sequential identifiers as defence in depth (never as the only control).
Add negative authorization tests (user A cannot read user B) to CI.
verify: Repeat the request with a second low-privilege account; the API must return 403/404.
Automated authorization test suite passes.
broken-access-control.detect: SOC: alert on a single session enumerating many object IDs in a short window.

auth-weakness.title: Weak authentication controls (no lockout / no MFA / weak policy)
fix: Put the application behind the corporate IdP (SSO) and enforce phishing-resistant MFA for all users, mandatory for admins.
Configure progressive delays or temporary lockout after repeated failures, plus breached-password screening.
Align password length and rotation rules with the corporate identity policy (length over complexity).
verify: Ten failed logins in a row trigger delay/lockout and a SIEM event.
Login without the second factor is refused for the test account.
auth-weakness.detect: SOC: password-spray and impossible-travel analytics on the IdP logs.

default-credentials.title: Default or vendor credentials accepted
fix: Change the default credential immediately to a unique secret stored in the corporate vault (PAM).
Disable or rename the vendor account if the product allows it.
Add a 'no default credentials' gate to the build/commissioning checklist for new devices.
verify: Login with the vendor default must fail.
Vault entry exists and rotation policy is attached.
default-credentials.detect: SOC: alert on any successful login with a known vendor account name.

security-misconfiguration-web.title: Missing web security headers / insecure cookie attributes
fix: Add Strict-Transport-Security (max-age >= 1 year), Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options and frame-ancestors at the reverse proxy for all virtual hosts.
Set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite on session cookies in the framework configuration.
Keep the header set in a shared proxy snippet under version control.
verify: curl -sI https://<host> shows the headers; ZAP passive scan shows no header alerts.
Browser dev tools show the cookie flags.
security-misconfiguration-web.detect: Track through configuration compliance; no SOC rule needed.

admin-interface-exposed.title: Administrative interface exposed to users or internet
fix: Move the admin path to an internal-only listener or restrict it by source IP at the reverse proxy.
Require SSO + MFA for the admin role.
Remove sample/installer pages left by the vendor.
verify: External request to the admin path returns 403/404.
Admin access works from the admin network with MFA.
admin-interface-exposed.detect: SOC: alert on admin path access from external IPs.

sensitive-data-exposure.title: Sensitive or personal data exposed (public storage, backups, listings)
fix: Remove public access to the storage/backup location immediately and keep a copy of access logs as evidence.
Rotate any secrets found inside the exposed files.
DPO assesses whether personal data was accessed and whether a GDPR Art. 33 notification (72 hours) is required.
Enable encryption at rest and a policy that blocks public buckets/shares by default.
verify: Anonymous request to the object/share URL returns 403.
Cloud posture scan shows the 'block public access' control enabled.
sensitive-data-exposure.detect: SOC: review access logs for the exposure window; alert on future public ACL changes.

logging-detection-gap.title: Attack activity not detected or not logged
fix: Onboard the missing log source (host, firewall, application) to the SIEM with parsing validated.
Create or tune the detection for the ATT&CK techniques used during the test, using the ATT&CK v20 detection strategies as a starting point.
Add the scenario to the purple-team regression list.
verify: Replay the test activity (atomic test) and confirm an alert is raised and triaged within the SOC SLA.
logging-detection-gap.detect: This ticket IS the detection work.

phishing-susceptibility.title: Users susceptible to phishing / social engineering
fix: Run short, role-based awareness sessions for the affected teams within 30 days (no blame, focus on reporting).
Deploy a one-click 'report phishing' button and publish the reporting channel.
Enforce MFA so a captured password alone is not enough.
Schedule a follow-up simulation in 90 days to measure improvement.
verify: Follow-up simulation click rate below the agreed target; report rate above target.
phishing-susceptibility.detect: SOC: triage queue for user-reported phishing with SLA.

impact_phrases.infra: an attacker could take control of the server and use it as a foothold for lateral movement or ransomware
impact_phrases.network: an attacker could reach internal systems directly from an untrusted network
impact_phrases.ot: an attacker could read or change process values or controller logic, with possible safety, environmental and production-loss consequences
impact_phrases.appsec: an attacker could read or modify application data and act as other users
impact_phrases.iam: an attacker could log in as a legitimate user and bypass most other controls
impact_phrases.data: confidential or personal data could be read by unauthorised parties, with regulatory exposure (GDPR)
impact_phrases.soc: an intrusion could progress without being noticed, increasing dwell time and damage
impact_phrases.people: attackers could obtain credentials or code execution through users
